tips.comment: Cost a bit at 50k and related to so many winners. Skelton's have a good one here and should be able to win on debut. Conditions to suit.

Hey Buddy is related to horses that have had some success in similar conditions and have won over hurdles at 2m. The trainer Fergal O'Brien has a solid reputation with newcomers, and horses from this stable often perform well in debut races.

A few in this race catch the eye including the Skelton's Dutch Corner who is a half brother to the high class but quirky Yorkhill, but at the odds and with a lovely pedigree I like the look of Not At That Price. He is a full brother to the very promising Let It Rain. The trainer Charlie Longsdon doesn't have many bumper runners, but does very well in these races.

Ivane would be the safer and more consistent pick for the Class 5 Hurdle Handicap race, given his solid finish in similar races. Scorsese's form in this race type is more erratic, which makes Ivane a better option for this specific race.

Caught the eye last time on just second start of the season and was bang in contention before fading late on. Handles good ground so conditions should be okay and did come good last year around this time of year as had form figures of 1321 from January to March. Is only 3lb higher than that last win of a handicap hurdle at Huntingdon last March. Yard in fair form with a couple of winners from the last ten sent out and my fancy should strip fitter now and can run a big race over a trip that suits. Doesn't look the deepest race and looks fairly handicapped on best form so as best form around this time of year is a cracking price now.

Finished a good 3rd of 13 last time out in a same as today class 5 over a maybe too short 2m 48yds as he was making late headway. The run before last was over 2m 3f where he was still going well when falling 3 out. Both of those runs were off a rating of 80, which drops to 79 today over a suitable trip of 2m 4f 88yds with A Wedge returning to the saddle.

Switches back to a left-hand track after two sub-standard runs around right-handers. Has better form around the lefties, so the hope is that a trip to Southwell will suit. Drops to a mark of 78, and both jockey and trainer are in good form. Still 3 places with a couple of firms available at the time of writing. NB
Shant Wait is a lightly raced gelding with early promise, and despite a disappointing handicap debut earlier this month, he remains unexposed and could improve with experience.
Pulled up the previous two times but had shown good enough form to improve if conditions are suitable. Has those conditions now.

I Maximus looks a big runner in this 6f maiden. He ran a nice race at Kempton last year when second and the soft ground probably caught him out next time at Newbury. Back on the all-weather now with a decent rating and a bit of experience, he sets the bar here. If he’s ready to roll after the break, he’s got a good shot at getting the job done.
Happy to take on the hot pot here, with Blue Rc (related to Invincible Speed who wasn't bad) coming here for the top combo of Clifford Lee and James Tate.
Finished unplaced last time out, but too many winners to count have come out of that race since, even a listed placed horse. It's solid form, and the horse is related to an all-weather winner.

Race 1 at Chelmsford City today is the British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race) (Class 5) for 3 to 5-year-olds over 1,207 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 3yo filly Cooramook from the Harry Eustace yard and will be ridden by in-form jockey Hayley Turner. This daughter of Mehmas had a moderate debut, then showed good improvement in her next race when finishing just over 3 lengths off the winner. Signs are that more improvement is likely, which puts her firmly in with a top chance for victory.

I'm taking a chance on Sir Kenny here at a massive price. Sir Kenny has only had one run thus far, finishing last, running green over a mile at Bath in October on soft/heavy ground. He has had a lot of time to mature since then and has had wind surgery and been gelded. Dylan Cunha has his string in fine form at the moment, and with the bare 8 in this field, he has a chance of a place at least.

Blue Sky Boy has been there or thereabouts a few times in recent runs and his close second here in January reads well. Last time at Southwell he didn’t quite see out the two miles, so this drop back in trip looks ideal. If he gets a decent pace to aim at, he’s got a solid chance of finally getting his nose in front.
Five-year-old has run well in defeat, although the latest run at Kempton is best forgotten when given a bit too much to get involved. Better expected here.
Likely to welcome the return to this course and distance, being a short head runner-up when last here 3 races back, and following 2 runs over this trip on the Southwell Tapeta.
Placed in a couple of races over 2f shorter recently. Looks like the extra distance could help and still improving.
Been given a low handicap mark. Has had 3 runs before this, showing ability in those, and should go well on the AW.

Might be worth an interest on this three-year-old who starts out with the McEntee yard. It has a positive jockey booking, and the change in surface might just see this make a winning start for the stable.

Showed plenty of promise in five races as a 2-y-o, and should be better for her first run in a handicap in February having been absent since November. She could also find extra for the first time headgear today.

Bust A Moon looks well in at the weights here and looks a leading player on form. Trainer/jockey combo are 4/8 at this track and 23% together overall. Makes debut for new stable that shows a 26pts profit at this track.

Double Mocha lines up in the 6:30 at Chelmsford and could be one to watch now switching to handicaps. He’s shown just enough in his novice runs to think there’s a bit more to come, and the trip and surface should suit. The hood stays on, Harry Davies takes 3lb off, and if he finds a bit of improvement, he’s got a chance of sneaking into the frame at a decent price.
3 average runs so far, but has been given a low mark by the handicapper and might be more capable of going in today at this course and distance.

General Assembly Won last time out over 5f at Wolverhampton, responding well to aggressive tactics. He holds a good record at the distance, only 2lb higher than his last win, and he's wearing cheekpieces for the first time which could bring further improvement.
Alafdhal hit the crossbar last time and is turned out again quickly. Has won at the course 4 times (although not at this distance) but course form should never be ignored here.
Went okay at Southwell recently. Needs to improve but has won over CD, and this looks like a winnable race.

Dark Side Prince returns to Chelmsford for the 7:00 race, aiming to defend his title after winning this event last year. With five course-and-distance victories under his belt, he clearly thrives on this track. Although his recent form has dipped, his current mark is appealing, and a return to familiar surroundings might reignite his spark. If he can recapture his previous form here, he’s got a solid chance of making his presence felt.

On a lengthy losing run but numbers a course and distance success among her seven career wins, and that off a seven pounds higher mark than today. The handicapper has given her a chance as she's competing off her lowest mark since 2022, and her double-figure odds could prove generous.

Birkenhead has had a couple of runs since the break and was not far away when fifth last time out off a 67. With a drop to a 66 today, He is worth a shot having last won on turf off a 67 and worth an EW.

A small each-way on the outsider of the field as things stand. Returns to the all-weather having spent much of last year running on the grass, including 2 victories at Brighton. Last AW success came at Wolverhampton back in '21. Small chance taken that the flat form can be converted into better performances over this surface.
Made a promising return in January when third, and this C&D winner looks well treated here. Has the draw to be handy and a good jockey booking.

Stella Hogan has been in strong form under Mick Appleby, with two wins and three places in her last five runs. She performs well at Chelmsford and faces a slightly weaker field today, increasing her chances. Consistency and track suitability make her a solid betting option.
This is the trainer's only entry he's got out today as they are stepping it back up to 7f with the same jockey on board. A good value each way bet.

Kondratiev Wave has not been far away for most runs this year, being placed three times out of five runs, and gets Rossa Ryan this time, which might be enough to get back on the top step while still running off a 60 EW.

Thomas Equinas goes in the 7:30 at Chelmsford and could be ready to bounce back. He got the job done over 7f at Wolves in November and hasn’t been far off in a few runs since. If he gets a bit of luck in running and finds that earlier form, he’s got every chance of getting involved off his current mark.

Got No Dollars has placed in 9 of 16 races at this course and has won 1 of 3 races with Sam Feilden in the saddle. He has good AW pedigree as progeny of Showcasing and Canada Water (Dansili). Last win was at the course off 1lb lower and stepping down in trip here.
Has got the draw to bounce out, go forward and control the pace of this race. Has been rated much higher than this and should at least place.
Won three times this year. Beaten favorite last time, odds on. Course and distance winner. Good jockey on board. Has to be shortlist material. Nap win.

Where's Freddy has won 3 times at 7f and has placed in 2 of 5 at this distance. He has good AW pedigree as progeny of Lope De Vega and One Spirit (Invincible Spirit). He has a good draw and has finished races strongly this season, with the booking of Rossa Ryan a bonus.
This one will be fitter for last time out run as they are dropping it down in grade with an interesting 5 lbs claiming jockey booking/change. A good value each way bet for the 4 places available.

This horse has had some issues in training, judging by the small amount of starts, but his last run in Southwell was very promising. They went off quite fast, and he was in the leading trio all the way to the line. Possibilities.
Half-brother to six horses, all of high ability. Has only had 4 runs and placed twice in them. This course and distance should suit and he should win.

A handicap without much depth, and Billy Mill appeals at double-figure odds. He has dropped to a good mark, and the step up in trip looks like a good move. He wasn't beaten far here on his last visit in a much stronger race than this and off a higher mark. He looks 5-star nap material.

Swiss Ace could run better than recent form suggests. He’s been a bit quiet lately but has some solid all-weather wins in the book and is back down to a workable mark. If he gets a good pace to aim at and things fall right, he’s definitely capable of landing a blow. Worth having an interest at big odds.

Didn't run well on Tapeta debut last time, but her penultimate start, her first run for 6 months, was a promising effort. She is now dropped in grade, the lowest grade she has raced in since winning a similar race last summer, and has a jockey upgrade with Hornby taking over. Strong each-way chance.

Thought that GUNLOCK showed enough on stable debut last time out at Kempton, especially off the back of a break in the first-time headgear. One to keep an eye on for sure. The draw may be off-putting and is a negative, but if dropped in, maybe he can get involved. With the extra place, it's a bet worth taking.

A 3 time winner over this course and distance, this 6-year-old recently finished last in a handicap at Southwell just 13 days ago. While his chances of winning seem slim, he has performed well here in the past. Jockey Marco Ghiani, who has secured 56 victories and placed 144 times at this venue, adds to the appeal. At 66/1, he presents good value for an each-way bet.

3-year-old colt sired by Holy Roman Emperor has yet to get his head in front but ran a good race here over this distance back in December under this jockey. The breeding suggests that this is a surface that he likes, and I think he will go very close to getting off the mark in this, his 2nd handicap run, if he is close to full fitness after a break.

Out of Kameko and broke maiden tag at Lingfield over 8f 22 days ago. Has an opening mark of 75 and is upped a further 2f in trip today, donning a first-time tongue tie but is open to further improvement.

Must Believe might be worth a second look after a decent third over this course and distance last time out and seems to be attracting overnight support. He didn’t show much as a 2yo but looked more switched on on his return. If he builds on that, there’s definitely a run in him off this mark.

He won on his penultimate start at Lingfield and had placed in his 3 runs prior. He disappointed last time out when 5th of 6, but he tries out a new trip and is now down in class, so could run better.
Jim Crowley's only ride at Chelmsford tonight after a time away in the Gulf. The yard doesn't normally use this jockey - a pointer in itself?

Handicap debut up in trip. 3/1 fave last year when last out over 6, ridden by Ryan Moore, which could explain the price. Is it ready? Have not a clue. You need a crystal ball to guess. Johnston's always trying. Stable definite chance if ready. Worth a small, very small interest. Breeding suggests it should be its trip.

Hibernate steps up in trip today and might just find this distance more to his liking. He hasn’t made much noise so far, but the switch to 1m2f and the eye-catching booking of Rossa Ryan could help unlock a bit more.

Pessoa has five course wins here at Wolverhampton, with the last coming over 7 furlongs last week. He has previously won over today's 1m0.5f off a 3lbs higher mark. He has a 5lbs penalty for last week's win but has a great chance of going in again.
Voltaic appears to be on a quite handy mark of 52 for this and with Molly Gunn claiming 7lb I think there's a good e.w. chance to be had. Is top-rated on TS and 3rd rated on RPR.

Absolutely Not runs in the 5:00 at Wolverhampton and might have a bit more to offer now switching to handicaps. She shaped okay on debut here last year, and while her two runs this season haven’t set the world alight, they should have brought her on. Hollie Doyle booked is eye-catching, and off a low mark, she’s not one to dismiss lightly.
Well worth an Each Way shot on Annalee Lass here in this race. It managed a win the last time it raced at Wolves. Definitely could repeat this today at 13/2.
Went okay when third a couple of starts ago, and six of her last ten wins were at this track, so connections like to run her here. Well drawn.

HAAF A DIAMOND is speculative and in a race where the favourite is short enough and most are difficult to fancy, such boldness could be rewarded. The selection is a winner and has run to a mark of 60 in defeat. Off 44 today, the 5-y-o is nicely weighted if, and it is an if, she returns from her winter break fit and ready. It catches my eye that she is owner-bred and this is the time of year when playing 'guess the mare in foal' begins. Not over exposed on the AW, and a placing would be reward enough at the price.

Those keeping an eye on handicap marks might have spotted Possible Ambition at Wolverhampton. He has won off a 5-pound higher mark over a similar trip as recently as February of last year. He has disappointed since, but a lot of those runs were at tracks where he hasn’t shown his best, and his last creditable run was here. He has had time off the track for most of last year and the first couple of months of this, so it wouldn’t be unusual for a horse to have needed the run last time out. If he is back to his best, he is an incredible bet at the price.

L’Immortale is flying right now and looks a big player in the 5:35 race. He bolted up at Lingfield just a few days ago and finally looks like he’s figured things out since joining Jack Jones. Yes, there’s a penalty to shoulder, but if he runs to the same level, he’s going to take plenty of stopping. Hard to ignore in this mood.
The win choice is Ravenglass on an attractive mark, having won off much higher in the past. Two good runs here in March (1st/2nd) prove the selection's fitness and current form.

An each-way bet is advised on all-weather champion chasing jockey Billy Loughnane, who made a pleasing return to action earlier this month at Chelmsford when 3rd. Definite place claims on that showing.
Strange race this. Many of these really do struggle to win races. This one can be slow away but at least has won twice over CD, which can't be said for most of these.

Kept on well but didn’t reach the leaders when 4th of 9 beat 2 lengths over a mile at Newcastle 2 weeks ago. Drops a pound as a consequence, Aiden Brookes retains the ride and the extra half a furlong will be welcome.
Returned from a break with a good run when traveling well for a long way but had to race on the wide outside. Likely to come on for that, so looks each-way value at 14/1. Nap.
Ex-Irish that started off the year well. Unlucky in running, has run poorly last twice, but if back to the form of the January run, then has an each-way chance.

At the odds, Stoic Syd might be more of an eachway contender. Ran well in defeat when finishing 5th in a Classified event last time out, if anything today's race is easier so it wouldn't be a surprise to see this horse do a bit better today.

Small eachway tip for Liege who wasn't at best form last time out but that was a better race than this last time, may find this easier and the step up in distance may be more suitable. Drawn well today, not badly treated.

Van Zant could run well if he’s on a going day. He grabbed a win at Southwell off today's mark a couple of months back and hasn’t been too far off since. He’s not the most consistent, but this kind of race suits and if things fall right, he’s definitely capable of getting involved.

HOT CASH has won a race at 7f. Fourth in a Group 3 race over 7f at Deauville on his latest outing in August last year. Upped in trip to 1m 1f and the surface should suit. Dropped in class and could well be able to win this race.

Even though Circus of Rome has shortened dramatically in the opening betting, I am not sure that the gelding needs the step up in trip. I am still siding with Marco Botti's Perfect Life. The colt beat a John Gosden horse at Wolverhampton in December. Perfect Life drops 3 pounds for that win today.

There’s potentially not an unobtainable standard set here by those with some runs, so the newcomers here I thought were worth a look. Camtank intrigued the most down the bottom, as not much in her pedigree other than her sire would suggest she would want this extended trip. She is half related to some winners at the trip, so there’s a chance she gets it. She’s thrown into it on debut getting all the allowances, and with Haggas being 7/8 a place (4 wins) with first-time-out 3-year-olds in the spring, there’s a fair chance she can mix it in here on that alone. So at the odds, I’m going to have a small play in the dark.
Way overpriced, this one. Only three starts and finished second to a well-fancied Gosden horse who had proven form in the book. Big chance of going in.

A Waldgeist gelding whose dam has achieved victory at 1 mile 9 furlongs. It's advisable to monitor the market as he makes his debut. However, given the stable's strong performance and jockey Dan Muscutt's notable experience, with 79 wins and 200 places here at Wolverhampton, an each-way wager at 40/1 offers fantastic value.

Risky tip so just a small eachway chance, the good odds are the main reason for this tip. Wasn't a terrible run when finishing 4th last time out, today's race is tougher but not by much. This horse should have more to offer in time so may at least run better than what these odds suggest. Drawn well
Had been touted by the yard as a great hope for the future and that didn't come to fruition last season, but certainly represents a value bet here in this company.

Very unlucky last time on a return from a break and should have come on plenty for it. The switch to Wolves is significant here as it's a track that has suited him better in the past. As a well-handicapped horse now, he could prove difficult to beat.

5f sprints here are more dependent on pure luck than the skill and talent of horses and jockeys. Cinque Verde won here back in January, beating a few of today's rivals in the process. She was raced over further next, but today she's back where she tasted success the last time, only up 1lb for that.

BANG ON THE BELL has won nine races from 5f to 6f. Fifth over 5f at Chelmsford City on his latest outing last month. Course, distance, and surface should suit. Seems well treated and could well be able to win this race.

Ecclesiastical notched a solid win over 5f at Lingfield earlier this month, and he’s no stranger to success here, having also bagged a course-and-distance victory last September. Jason Hart gets back on, he’s clearly thriving, and while there’s a bit more weight to carry, he’s in the kind of form where that might not matter.

Hopefully, the breaks appear for Dashing Harry to be accountable with coming back to five furlongs and racing off 74, which he won off at Lingfield, where he held One Night Stand and Night On Earth, who finished second and third.

Previous course and distance winner back here in September and has finished runner up on last two outings. Raised one pound after the Wolverhampton 2nd on Feb 10th. Both jockey and trainer in reasonable form. Has the widest draw to contend with, which could be the biggest issue to overcome. Cinque Verde and Reigning Profit seem the two biggest threats. Good each-way chance.

Lightly raced 5yo. He was a close runner-up two starts back, which was a first try over this 12f trip. A bit below par last time out but is now running in an amateur riders’ handicap with a good jockey booking. On a good looking mark and is unexposed on the polytrack surface.

Three career runs for the 3yo. His best effort was last time out at this track over 8f, polytrack debut. He showed a high cruising speed, had his rivals struggling 2f out, looked set to win entering the final furlong, but ran out of gas in the last 100 yards. On a handy looking mark for his handicap debut and the drop down to 7f should help.

Four runs this winter for the 6yo, two respectable efforts. Far too keen four weeks ago when beaten 2L but he has dropped another 3lb after that effort and he was rated 10lb higher just four runs back. He could be overpriced in this low grade contest.

The 3-year-old filly has not been beaten far in her five runs since last October, three times over this 5f C/D. On a reduced mark now, a good 3lb claiming jockey helping his chances, will be fresh after a six-week break and is drawn in stall 1.

The 4yo has been progressive this winter, four wins since Dec and only 3lb higher than his last win. Beaten a length last time out but didn’t get a clear passage. Decent draw for this 6f contest, good jockey change and can go well again.

Starmount has already got some decent Point-to-Point form from Ireland, and he is well related, being a half-brother to Stage Star. Ben Pauling has talked about this horse very favorably, and he had a nice bumper winner at Southwell today, so continues in good form.

A progressive 4yo who has won or been placed in 9 of 14 races. Coming off a 4 month break but the yard is having a very good year so far and he should be ready. A good apprentice in the saddle whose 5lb claim is a big plus. The recent break and a gelding op could easily bring about more improvement.

The 5-year-old lost by a neck in this Listed contest last year after coming off an 8-month break, beaten by a subsequent Group 1 winner. Not great in three following races last summer. However, he arrives here after three big runs on the AW already this year, and fitness could play a big part.

The 4-year-old is coming off a 5-month break, but he was a close 2nd of 13 in a French Group 1 race on his return last year. Things did not really go to plan after, finishing 6th of 16 in the Derby and 4th of 12 in a quality Group 1 when last seen. He’s had time to get his act together and can be a big player at this Listed level.

He finished last season with two nice runs and two 100+ RPR ratings. He went very close on the AW three weeks ago, after a 5 month break, and his well-being seems fine. No problem with the slower ground. On a decent mark. Few miles on the clock for the 4yo and plenty of room for more progress.

The 4yo has 1 win from 7. Progressed nicely last year, running well in defeat and not beaten far when last seen in a useful £52K turf handicap. Improvement possible after 5 months off the track. Weighted to go well and strong jockey booking. Question marks against most of these rivals.

Unexposed 4yo. Four career runs, form 2213. Two narrow defeats at this track to start his career. A 9L turf maiden win on his third start. Posted a good RPR rating when last seen, which was a decent class 2 turf handicap. Nice mark, 7 months off the track but could have a decent future.

Just four career runs for the 4yo. She missed all last year, but she was a very close runner-up in a Group 1 when last seen and can be a player in this Listed contest. She easily has the second highest rating, and the short-priced favorite is coming back from a 5-month break.
